skill.name: reactome-database
skill.description: Use Reactome REST APIs and helper scripts to query pathways, map genes, run enrichment analysis, and inspect biological results.
skill.summary: Query Reactome APIs for pathway lookup, gene enrichment, expression analysis, and result visualization.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses Reactome REST endpoints and a helper script to submit identifiers, retrieve tokens, and build browser URLs. No prompt injection, credential access, or malicious command execution was found; most high and medium static hits are Markdown or URL parsing false positives. The main actionable risks are expected third-party data submission and one helper-script file write that can overwrite a user-derived results path.

remediation.issue: Reactome analysis sends user identifiers or expression data to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning before live analysis and advise users not to submit restricted or patient-linked data without approval.

remediation.issue: scripts/reactome_query.py writes results to a filename derived from the input path.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit output argument, refuse overwrites by default, and require a force option for replacement.

remediation.issue: Requests examples and helper methods do not set network timeouts.
remediation.suggestion: Add reasonable timeouts and retry guidance so API failures do not hang long-running analysis workflows.

content.value_statement: Biology teams need fast access to curated pathway context for genes, proteins, and expression tables. This skill guides Reactome API queries, enrichment analysis, token retrieval, and browser review.
actual_capabilities: Query Reactome Content Service for pathway, reaction, complex, and entity records.
Run overrepresentation analysis for gene or protein identifier lists.
Submit expression tables to Reactome Analysis Service examples.
Retrieve analysis results by seven-day tokens.
Use scripts/reactome_query.py for version, query, search, entities, and analyze commands.
Build Reactome Pathway Browser URLs for analysis review.
limitations: Requires network access to reactome.org for live queries and analysis.
Submits identifiers or expression data to an external Reactome service.
The helper script has limited output path controls and overwrites generated result files.
reactome2py is noted as functional but not actively maintained.

use_cases.title: Prioritize enriched pathways
use_cases.description: Analyze a gene or protein list and identify Reactome pathways with significant enrichment metrics.

use_cases.title: Interpret pathway membership
use_cases.description: Look up a pathway ID and review participating proteins, complexes, reactions, and species context.

use_cases.title: Automate reproducible pathway checks
use_cases.description: Use the helper script to query versions, search pathways, and save repeatable analysis outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Look up a pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome database skill to summarize pathway R-HSA-69278, including name, species, major entities, and a browser link.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a gene list
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, MYC, and CDK1 for enriched Reactome pathways. Highlight significant results and unmapped identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Review expression results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this expression table with Reactome analysis. Explain the strongest pathways, FDR values, and genes that drive each result.

prompt_templates.title: Design a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Reactome pathway analysis workflow for a lab dataset. Include input validation, privacy warnings, token reuse, and output file naming.

output_examples.input: Gene list: TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, MYC, and CDK1.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes enriched cell cycle and DNA repair pathways, lists significant FDR values, and notes identifiers that did not map.
The response explains the pathway name, species, entity types, core participating molecules, and where to open the pathway browser view.

output_examples.input: Expression table with three samples and gene-level values.
output_examples.output: The response describes the top Reactome pathways, interprets expression-associated signals, and records the analysis token for later retrieval.

best_practices: Confirm users can share gene lists before submitting them to Reactome.
Use batch analysis and token retrieval instead of repeated single-gene requests.
Set explicit output names and archive the Reactome database version with results.
anti_patterns: Do not submit unpublished clinical or patient-linked data without approval.
Do not treat pathway enrichment as causal proof without biological validation.
Do not rerun large analyses when a valid Reactome token can retrieve results.

faq.question: What is Reactome?
faq.answer: Reactome is a curated pathway database for reactions, proteins, complexes, small molecules, and biological processes.

faq.question: Does this skill need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. Live pathway queries and enrichment analysis require requests to reactome.org services.

faq.question: Can it analyze expression data?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents Reactome expression analysis format and submission through the Analysis Service.

faq.question: Are results stored locally?
faq.answer: The helper script saves full analysis results beside the input file using a derived filename.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is private data sent outside my environment?
faq.answer: Yes, if you run live analysis. Gene lists or expression values are submitted to Reactome.
